key_insight: For shape-informed hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and finite-element physical consistency are more effective during fine-tuning than during initial training.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields, advancing surrogate modeling toward rapid cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate physiologically consistent CFD data from SynthAorta geometries using automatic boundary-condition adjustment.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields on a common reference geometry and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Fine-tune with active learning and differentiable finite-element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: Peak-systolic field evaluations show fine-tuning benefits from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition, while out-of-distribution tests identify geometric coverage as the primary limitation.
watch_item: Generalization remains limited by the geometric support of the anatomy parametrization; changing network architecture alone may not resolve this.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
